rawVariants.cite: OV 2110-0:2018-SMPTE, ST 2110, “Professional Media Over Managed IP Networks Roadmap for the 2110 Document Suite (SMPTE Overview Document),” OV 2110-0:2018, pp. 1–4, Accessed: Jan. 24, 2019, doi: 10.5594/SMPTE.OV2110-0.2018. used pieces of kit as well as software is essential when configuring or debugging an environment like this. What Could be Improved? A lot of configuration work is required to set up all the components. An environment like this can be scaled up, although deployment tools seem to be quickly becoming a necessity to easily deploy the Embrionix SFPs, for example. For the kind of programs that would be created with a software-based studio at VRT, it seems feasible to use the vision switcher as a GUI on a touch screen. For audio processing, a physical panel with buttons and sliders will do for now. The cumulative delay between the incoming feed and the processed output is somewhat high compared to the parallel SDI-based control room. A software-based intercom solution is still missing from this setup. Overall With a good understanding of the underlying technologies, this setup was fairly easy to implement. It offers similar business benefits to the first project, plus the ability to share resources, reuse, and reconfigure the entire setup on the fly. The ease of use brought by the AMWA interface specifications is not to be underestimated. It can be compared to the phasing out of the “hello girls”43 in favor of the automatic telephony exchange. Conclusion Workflows Changes in the market are coming very quickly, with a clear direction toward software. From a technical point of view, the transition to software has started at the lower layers: the data plane and the control plane. From the perspective of more efficient operational workflows, it was determined that changing the physical controls to a GUI would have a much larger and immediately tangible impact, allowing many functions to be combined and consequently freeing up additional manpower to create more programs. While the first project relied on some software development, the second project solely relies on configuration. Services are configured and connected to each other in a user-friendly interface. In terms of skills, this is a bonus, lowering the threshold for using this type of application. Not all broadcast engineers have software development skills, nor do all developers have a solid broadcast background. Being able to understand correctly what a director wants to configure, the environment seems to be the new challenge of support. To achieve a new level of operational efficiency with VRT’s production environment, which needs to be flexible, scalable, and shareable for both recurring and one-off productions, software-based production seems to be the direction to take when building our new facility. A lot of productions will benefit tremendously from using graphical user interfaces. Nevertheless, there will still be a need for tactile interfaces for use-cases such as sports and other big high value productions.
